HANDOFF — Track I mirror-remediation epic `undamaged-murderous-horse` (f79d-0d71-0fd7-439f).

## Where this stands

15 children: 3 CLOSED (F1 refutable-goosebumpy-opossum, F12 classical-grey-ayeaye, F13 misandrous-defaceable-zenaida — all merged), 6 IN PROGRESS with changes on Gerrit, 6 OPEN.

Six-change Gerrit stack, all `LLM-Review +1` and all `Verified -1` — the reviews passed, only CI is red:

| change | ticket | subject |
|---|---|---|
| 2530 | e755-9371-7951-454a (F3) | Partition ticket types for the plan-review gate |
| 2531 | 62eb-5e6f-512a-420d (F5) | Derive the MCP model registry, compare enums |
| 2533 | a516-e61b-ede9-465c (F6) | Derive the reducer's status vocabulary |
| 2535 | cacb-8d57-efff-4ab1 (F4) | Derive cycle-capable relations from one set |
| 2536 | ce8f-4da9-2836-4115 (F7) | Derive create's ticket-type vocabulary |
| 2537 | 6850-af5c-a4a1-4c5d (F2) | Derive the op-cert kind vocabulary |

Change 2534 is ABANDONED — a duplicate I created by re-committing instead of amending, which minted a fresh Change-Id. 2535 is its live replacement.

## The two open CI failures (root causes NOT yet confirmed)

1. **2530: job `require resolvable rebar ticket` FAILED.** Locally `rebar resolve e755-9371-7951-454a` succeeds and the trailer is well-formed, so the leading hypothesis is that the ticket is not VISIBLE to CI — the `tickets` branch may not have reached `origin`. Unverified.
2. **2537 (and others): pytest FAILED in ~50s.** That is fast enough to be a collection/import error rather than a slow test. It does NOT reproduce locally (`import rebar.opcert_service.jobs; import rebar._commands.remote_cert` succeeds here). Recent suspects: `from rebar.signing import OPCERT_KINDS` added to both `opcert_service/jobs.py` and `_commands/remote_cert.py`, and `_VALID_KINDS` moved above `_USAGE` in remote_cert. Unverified — needs the real CI log.

## Attestation state of the unlanded children

- `weedy-ivory-tahr` (F9, 70f5) — CERTIFIED, claimed, being implemented in an isolated worktree.
- `glistening-dying-diplodocus` (F8, 91b0) — CERTIFIED, not yet claimed. Ready to implement.
- `eagleeyed-commutable-mantisray` (bc66) — unsigned; its plan review was still running.
- `elfin-decagonal-polarbear` (F11, 1daf) — unsigned, and BLOCKED: it `depends_on` bc66 and reads `ready_to_work: false`.
- `evolved-secluded-serpent` (F10, a691) and `immoderate-angelic-ibis` (F14, 0af1) — plans written with acceptance criteria, testing sections and file_impact recorded, but NEVER REVIEWED yet.

## Automation left running (session-only; dies with this session)

- Cron job `46e3b0eb`, firing :07/:27/:47, one increment per tick: harvest finished reviews, land green changes, close merged tickets, start the next mirror in dependency order. Auto-expires after 7 days. `CronDelete 46e3b0eb` stops it.
- Two subagents: one owns `/Users/joeoakhart/track-i-defect-introduction` and is driving the six-change stack to green; one is in its own isolated worktree implementing F9 and will push it as an INDEPENDENT change off origin/main.

## Hazards a successor must know

- **The 800-LOC module cap runs in CI, NOT in `make lint`.** Five `src/rebar` files sit at EXACTLY 800: `_commands/composer.py`, `_cli/_registry.py`, `llm/plan_review/sizing.py`, `llm/plan_review/sidecar.py`, `_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli.py`. Adding one line to any of them reddens the whole stack. Check with `find src/rebar -name "*.py" -exec wc -l {} + | awk '$1>800'` before editing. This already cost this epic one Verified -1 and one botched recovery.
- **Record `file_impact` BEFORE running `review-plan`.** Setting it afterwards invalidates the attestation (`file_impact 0 -> N paths`) and `sign-review` correctly refuses to re-sign across a changed plan. That cost three re-reviews.
- **Amend, never re-commit.** Re-committing a change that already has a Change-Id opens a duplicate Gerrit change (that is how 2534 happened).
- **Deriving a value is not automatically safe.** Two near-misses: `sorted()` in F7 would have silently reordered user-facing help text (`get_args` preserves declaration order); and in F2 the canonical `OPCERT_KINDS` is an unordered frozenset while both copies are ordered tuples feeding argparse `choices=`, an API error message, and a public `__all__` export.
- **Check import direction before "generate-from-canonical".** F1 and F9 both turned out to need an assertion or a deferred import rather than a direct derivation, because the canonical module was the DEPENDENT, not the leaf.

## Filed along the way, outside the epic

- `cyclopean-bloodshot-hoatzin` (3276-2f81-8c75-4ddd) — the root-disk outage bug; another session owns it.
- `tomophobic-ambient-killdeer` (414e-44bf-d1ff-4e13) — the plan-review deterministic floor is not deterministic: three identically-shaped siblings, two BLOCKED for missing acceptance criteria and one PASSED AND SIGNED with `coverage.llm_ran=true`.
- `lowly-lawrencium-ovenbird` (3a02-66ea-9229-470c) — 41 undeclared MCP schema properties across four models, baselined by F5 rather than bundled into a gate change because declaring them alters the published `outputSchema`.
